clue.text: Shake one's booty in place where miners were confined? The lowest of the low

parts.note: to rock something is to shake it back and forth
booty is slang for the buttocks, so one's booty is one's bottom

explanation.surface: A dance instruction collides with the Chilean miners trapped deep underground in 2010.
explanation.walkthrough: A third reading sits in the middle: the miners were confined at the very bottom of the rock, so the whole phrase also describes where they were.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically, hitting the absolute lowest point or level is reaching that extreme depth.

clue.text: Form of torture reported in three quarters of Iraq, according to Americans

indicators.note: reported signals a word as it is spoken
Americans say the country's name with a short a, rhyming with back
three quarters of a four-letter word is its last three letters

explanation.surface: A news item on torture claims in Iraq, as told by Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: The British say 'ir-AHK'; the American pronunciation of the last three letters matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The rack was a frame that stretched a victim's limbs, a medieval torture device.

clue.text: Cameron reformed expensive fiddle

indicators.note: reformed means formed again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: David Cameron's reforms as a costly piece of political trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like a swindle; it is a violin. Italian violins from this town fetch huge prices.
explanation.definitionFit: Instruments made in the Italian city by Stradivari and Amati are prized and costly violins.

clue.text: Leads from broadcaster inadvertently picked up someone expressing prejudiced views

indicators.note: leads are front letters, taken from the two words

parts.note: got means obtained or picked up

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown's 2010 gaffe, when a live microphone caught him calling a voter a bigoted woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigot holds intolerant opinions about other groups and voices them.

clue.text: Counted cost of big bomb

parts.note: tall means big in height
IED is an improvised explosive device, a roadside bomb

explanation.surface: Assessing what a large bomb attack cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallying is keeping a count, so tallied means added up or reckoned.

clue.text: Chief taxman robs one outrageously

indicators.note: outrageously suggests wild disorder, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: The head of the tax office robs someone shamelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: George Osborne was Chancellor of the Exchequer from 2010, the minister in charge of taxation.

clue.text: Head of Wikileaks in examination of strike on Pakistani valley

indicators.note: in places the head letter inside the word for the examination

parts.note: SAT is a standard school assessment test

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A news item: a leaked report about a military strike on a valley in Pakistan.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also a word for strike, which the surface uses as a noun; the Pakistani valley is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swat valley is a region in the north-west of Pakistan, much in the news around 2010.

clue.text: Mistreat cat, say, and we'll get kind of cross

parts.note: to whip someone is to beat or mistreat them
a cat is an example of a pet

explanation.surface: Abuse a cat and we will get angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry; it means a cross-breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The whippet dog was bred by crossing greyhounds with terriers.

clue.text: Man putting golf, during row, before wife's love leads to overblown divorce settlement

indicators.note: before places that piece ahead of the rest
during puts the golf letter inside the row

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
W is the abbreviation for wife
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: leads to takes the first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A golfer's marriage row leads to a huge divorce payout.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiger Woods divorced in 2010 after reports of infidelity; 'putting' is golf's putting, not placing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger Woods is a famous golfer, a man who putts on the green.

clue.text: Instrument with very easy sound (for some) rising in the back of the throat?

indicators.note: in puts the turned letters inside the throat part

parts.note: the uvula hangs at the back of the throat

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters read upwards, backwards
for some, chiefly Americans, the letters E and Z sound like this word

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EZ

explanation.surface: A musical instrument whose easy noise rises from the throat.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the plastic horn made famous at the 2010 World Cup; 'for some' means the American shorthand that spells the word easy as two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The vuvuzela is a long plastic horn blown by South African football fans.

clue.text: Member in (primarily) Conservative Government…

indicators.note: in places the limb inside the two initial letters
primarily, in brackets, picks the first letters of the following two words

parts.note: a leg is a member, in the sense of a limb

explanation.surface: A description of the Liberal Democrat leader sitting in the 2010 coalition government.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the Deputy Prime Minister of the coalition, while the parse builds him from a limb inside the initials of the governing party and government.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick Clegg was Deputy Prime Minister, a Liberal Democrat member of the Conservative-led coalition.

clue.text: …which follows party holding power making heavy weather of things

indicators.note: follows puts the letter for which after the other pieces

parts.note: Labour is the British political party
a party in power is said to be in
which refers back to the previous clue's Government, giving its abbreviation G

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the coalition follows a long-serving party and is struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the one before, so 'which' stands for the Government there, abbreviated G.
explanation.definitionFit: Labouring a task is toiling at it with great effort, like struggling over something simple.

clue.text: Spill affecting oil sector — nothing's going to be more damaging

indicators.note: a spill sends the words' letters everywhere, so they are rearranged
going says the letter for nothing departs from the pool

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An oil spill hurting the industry, with nothing worse to come — or the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Take O from the letters of OIL SECTOR and rearrange the remaining eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something costlier carries a higher price or loss, so it does more harm.

clue.text: Ignoring inner circle, Pope gets into second half of tour — it's stimulating!

indicators.note: gets into puts the trimmed pontiff inside the end of the tour
second half of keeps the last two letters of the four-letter word
ignoring means leaving out the named letter

parts.note: the inner circle is the round letter O in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: The Pope's visit, minus his entourage, reaches the second leg of his tour, which is thrilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inner circle' looks like a group of papal advisers; it is the round letter in the middle of the pontiff's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a stimulant drug is an upper, so something stimulating fits.

clue.text: Bags with lots of pockets mean more than one place for al-Qaeda to conceal bomb

parts.words: mean more than one place for al-Qaeda to conceal bomb
parts.note: both words name hiding places for bombs: an aircraft's cargo hold and the underwear bomber's underpants

explanation.surface: Pocketed trousers suggest several spots where terrorists might hide explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: Bags is British slang for loose trousers. The 2010 parcel bombs went in cargo; the 2009 underwear bomber used his pants.
explanation.definitionFit: These loose trousers have big patch pockets on the thighs, like a soldier's.

clue.text: Alternative Vote caused trouble but proved useful

parts.note: AV is the abbreviation for the Alternative Vote electoral system
ailed means troubled or afflicted

explanation.surface: The Alternative Vote, a 2011 referendum topic, stirred up trouble but turned out helpful.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to be of use or benefit, so something that availed served well.

clue.text: 'Big Society', for starters, should entail generosity

parts.note: large means big

indicators.note: for starters picks the first letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Cameron's 'Big Society' slogan of 2010 should start with generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is liberal giving of money or gifts, open-handedness.

clue.text: Copy voter's final switch to bring in right

indicators.note: a final switch moves the end letter to a new spot
to bring in places that letter back inside the word

parts.note: an elector is a voter

explanation.surface: An electoral instruction: copy a voter's last-minute change to support the right.
explanation.walkthrough: ELECTOR becomes ELECTRO when its final R is shifted one place earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: An electro is short for an electrotype, a printing plate duplicated by electrolytic deposition.

clue.text: G Brown endlessly left to get embarrassed

indicators.note: endlessly removes the first and last letters of the name

parts.note: red means left-wing in politics

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown, out of office and leftist, ends up blushing.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow red is to blush, the reddening face that comes with embarrassment.

clue.text: Second of overs thrown — penalty introduced for pair of cricketers

indicators.note: introduced puts the penalty inside the remaining letters
second of names the second letter of the word
thrown means thrown out, so that letter goes

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a bowler's second over thrown away and a penalty awarded.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing V leaves OERS, with PEN inside after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: The two batsmen who start a cricket innings are the opening pair.

clue.text: Opposition from French surrounding important Sarkozy plan starts trade union rising

indicators.note: surrounding wraps the French word around the other pieces

parts.note: de is French for from

indicators.note: starts are the first letters of the three words
in a down clue rising means read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: French unions rise up against a major plan of President Sarkozy.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispute is a disagreement or argument, a clash of opposing sides.

clue.text: Cheryl, as far as Ashley's concerned, was being dramatic and made demands

parts.words: Cheryl, as far as Ashley's concerned
parts.note: Cheryl Cole is footballer Ashley Cole's former wife, his ex
acted means performed or played a part

explanation.surface: Celebrity gossip: Cheryl Cole made a scene in front of Ashley and laid down demands.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheryl Cole was a British pop star married to England footballer Ashley Cole until 2010.
explanation.definitionFit: Exacting something is demanding and obtaining it, so the past tense means insisted on.

clue.text: Give peerage to John Prescott finally — it'll mostly, primarially exemplificate upholding of English?

indicators.note: in a down clue the rest is held up beneath the English letter, which sits on top
finally picks the last letters of the two names
mostly drops the last letter of the word
a mangled form of primarily, it picks the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: John Prescott, famed for mangled English, is given a peerage, in his own style.
explanation.walkthrough: Prescott, a Labour deputy PM known for garbled speech, became a lord in 2010; the clue mimics his diction.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble someone confers a title on them, such as a peerage.

clue.text: Rome's defence in trial over party in which minors are admitted

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the trial above the rest

parts.note: a test is a trial
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, children allowed
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A legal case against Rome, about a party where under-age guests got in.
explanation.definitionFit: The testudo was the Roman legion's tortoise formation of interlocked shields.

clue.text: Obama's right-hand man rejected, butt of electorate's anger

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: veep is American slang for vice-president, Obama's deputy

indicators.note: the butt is the tail end, the last letter

explanation.surface: Obama's deputy is rebuffed and becomes the target of voters' fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butt' pretends to mean a target; it means the end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeve is an irritation, and to peeve is to annoy, close to anger.

clue.text: It's as designed — Brown trapped in 'I agree with Nick'

indicators.note: trapped in puts the colour inside the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown's televised 'I agree with Nick' in the 2010 debates, staged and cornered.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Nick is the Devil, so someone who agrees with Nick follows him.
explanation.definitionFit: A devil-worshipper sides with Old Nick, a traditional name for the Devil.

clue.text: Post union strike row — compromise deal terms

explanation.surface: After a union dispute and strike, a compromise deal is agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terms' looks like the conditions of a deal; it means the ends of the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A newel is the post at the top or bottom of a staircase.

clue.text: Odds on Afghans in firing ranges?

indicators.note: odds are the odd-numbered letters of the word

explanation.surface: Betting on Afghan forces at shooting ranges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firing ranges' looks military; these are cookers that are fired.
explanation.definitionFit: Aga is a brand of heavy range cooker, heated by a burning fuel.

clue.text: It's inevitable Mumsnet loses head, going mad about Miliband and Balls?

indicators.note: about places the rearranged letters around the two names
going mad means scrambled into disorder
loses head drops the first letter

parts.note: Ed Miliband and Ed Balls are two Eds

explanation.surface: Mumsnet, the parenting forum, is furious about the two Labour Eds, inevitably.
explanation.walkthrough: Mumsnet is a British parenting website; Ed Miliband and Ed Balls were leading Labour politicians in 2010.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'needs must' means one must do something because circumstances leave no choice.

clue.text: United no good after Wayne Rooney's initials extracted with difficulty

indicators.note: after puts the two initials before the rest
initials are the first letters of the two names

explanation.surface: Manchester United are poor once Wayne Rooney is prised away, painfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrung out, information or money is squeezed out by force or pressure.

clue.text: Band of volcanic matter going past Sweden

indicators.note: going past puts the ash after the country letter

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden
volcanic ash is matter ejected by eruptions

explanation.surface: A band of volcanic ash drifting past Sweden, as in the 2010 Icelandic eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist.

clue.text: In revolt about student debts, Liberal's surrounded: 'Rotten liar out!'

indicators.note: surrounded puts the remaining letters inside the others

parts.note: re means about or concerning
L is a learner, a student
IOUs are written promises to repay debts

out removes the jumbled word's letters from the party word

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotten' says the letters of the liar may come out of the party word in any order, not as a block.
